_about: The single source of truth for what Fleet Radar watches.
Read by: the Bright Data collectors (which URLs to scrape), the classifier
(which packages to reason about), and the correlation engine (how to match a
radar package back to the package names the agent actually reports).
Source pages are deliberately heterogeneous - official docs, vendor download
pages, GitHub releases, and endoflife.date - so the scrapers must handle
genuinely different page structures. That diversity is what makes the
self-healing demo meaningful rather than staged against one template.
STATUS: URLs below are provisional targets. Each one is verified when we
point a collector at it in Stage 2 (changelog) and Stage 3 (EOL).

packages._why: Ships on every Linux host and has a strict, well-published support window.
packages._version_granularity_note: Support and EOL are tracked per 3.x line, so 3.7.0 and 3.7.9 share a verdict.

changelog.notes: Release listing with version + release date per row.

eol.notes: Official status table: branch, status, first release, end of support.

packages._why: Best breaking-change signal in the watchlist - release notes have an explicit backwards-incompatible section.

changelog.notes: Release notes index; per-release pages carry the backwards-incompatible changes.

eol.notes: Supported-versions table plus an unsupported-versions list with end-of-life dates.

packages._why: Fixed LTS calendar makes EOL verdicts unambiguous and easy to defend on stage.
packages._version_granularity_note: Node support is tracked per major line (18.x, 20.x, 22.x).

changelog.notes: Blog-style release feed - structurally unlike the table-driven sources.

eol.notes: Official release schedule table with end-of-life dates per major line.

packages._why: The highest-stakes package here - an unsupported OpenSSL is a real security exposure, which is the impact story.

changelog.notes: Dense plain-text changelog - the hardest extraction target in the set.

eol.notes: Third-party aggregator; used where no single official EOL table exists.

packages._why: npm breadth. Carries a changelog signal only - no formal EOL calendar exists, which is itself a realistic case the pipeline must tolerate.

changelog.notes: GitHub releases page - a fourth distinct page structure.
